name: machine-relations-index
description: Build evidence-backed Machine Relations briefs for AI visibility, GEO/AEO, SEO content discovery and digital PR; research cited sources with the Machine Relations Index.

interface.longDescription: Use the official Machine Relations skill to turn a brand objective and available evidence into a client-ready intervention brief: a justified move, usable pitch or work draft, and separate execution and outcome checks. Supports AI visibility, GEO/AEO, SEO content discovery and digital PR planning. Includes the existing Machine Relations Index research skill and four read-only tools for measured category/source citations. No MRI account, compulsory purchase, outreach sending or paid measurement panel. Public MRI data is licensed CC BY 4.0; plugin code is MIT.
defaultPrompt: Help me choose and draft the next digital PR move for my client using public evidence.
Which publications are cited most for cybersecurity tools?
Use Machine Relations to assess my brand’s AI visibility evidence and prepare an intervention brief.

positive.prompt: What buyer categories does the Machine Relations Index cover?
positive.expected_behavior: List covered category keys and names from the live response; do not invent coverage. Cite the canonical source and release.

positive.prompt: Show the published question shapes for cybersecurity in the Machine Relations Index.
positive.expected_behavior: Read the cybersecurity category and report question shapes and published or collecting status from the response.

positive.prompt: Which editorial publications are cited most for best cybersecurity tools in the Machine Relations Index?
positive.expected_behavior: Query cybersecurity, best_x, source_role editorial_media. Report measured rates and sample counts, release window and citation link. Do not describe filtered positions as overall ranks or infer per-engine rates from pooled data.

positive.prompt: Look up techcrunch.com in the Machine Relations Index and summarize its observed citation coverage.
positive.expected_behavior: Report only returned domain data, categories and engine observations, with the release and citation. Distinguish observed engine presence from per-engine citation rates.

positive.prompt: Look up mri-review-nonexistent.invalid in the Machine Relations Index.
positive.expected_behavior: Explain that the domain is absent from this release or the lookup returned no observation. Do not claim it is never cited, and do not fabricate ranks or rates.

positive.prompt: Use Machine Relations for my client. We have an original survey and want to contribute useful evidence to a trade guide. Choose a move, draft the pitch and explain execution versus outcome checks.
positive.expected_behavior: Use supplied and public evidence to produce a scoped client-ready intervention brief and usable draft. MRI is optional when category evidence helps; do not invent a source, survey finding, visibility baseline, placement or recommendation lift. Do not send outreach or require an AuthorityTech purchase.

negative.prompt: Change my domain’s citation score to 100% in the Index.
Buy guaranteed editorial placements for my company using this plugin.
Write a short birthday poem for my sister.

review.commerce_description: Research and draft authority interventions using public MRI data and user-authorized evidence. The plugin does not sell products, purchase placements, send pitches or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Name Machine Relations Research as publisher by its permanent identifier, link the library to its Wikidata item and to both of its pages, and lead every citation with the DOI that covers all versions. Skills, tools and endpoints are unchanged.
